Per-socket RAPL energy on AMD EPYC (Zen) nodes, x86 builds only, same reader as intel_x86_rapl: perf power PMU event (scaled), else powercap energy_uj; no MSR access. Values are running totals in mJ since daemon start, modulo 2^32.
CPU package (socket) id from topology/physical_package_id, e.g. 0. One row per socket.
Energy of the socket's cores domain (perf energy-cores, else powercap core zone), mJ modulo 2^32. delta mJ / (1000 x elapsed s) = watts. -2 NOT_PRESENT when the kernel exposes no core domain.

AMD Genoa (Zen4) DRAM traffic from the Data Fabric amd_df uncore PMU via direct perf; x86 builds, enabled only when the runtime CPU is Genoa. One row per DRAM channel (12), each summing the PMU cpumask CPUs, so it covers all sockets (socket 0 only on el8 kernels). Read and write beats are counted separately.
chan<N>: DRAM channel row N of the amd_df PMU (chan0..chan11), summed over all sockets, e.g. chan0.
Not used on Genoa (Zen4): Zen4/Zen5 split traffic into dram_read_beats and dram_write_beats, so this key is always -2 NOT_PRESENT.
64-byte DRAM read data beats (local or remote socket) on this channel, modulo 2^48. Sum delta over all chan rows x 64 / elapsed s = node DRAM bytes/s.
64-byte DRAM write data beats (local or remote socket) on this channel, modulo 2^48. Sum delta over all chan rows x 64 / elapsed s = node DRAM bytes/s.

Nanoseconds this channel's events were enabled, summed over its events and cpumask CPUs, 64-bit. delta running / delta enabled = share of time the counters ran; below 1 the beat counts are scaled estimates. No solo key for uncore.

Nanoseconds this channel's events actually ran on a counter, summed over its events and cpumask CPUs, 64-bit. delta running / delta enabled = share of time the counters ran; below 1 the beat counts are scaled estimates. No solo key for uncore.

DRAM traffic on aarch64 (arm backend builds) via direct perf on memory uncore PMUs, scaled by enabled/running. BeeGFS client capacity and approximate I/O bytes per mount. Mounts of type beegfs or beegfs_nodev come from /proc/mounts; capacity from statvfs on the mount dir each sample; bytes from kernel TCP counters on connections to servers in /proc/fs/beegfs/<inst>/storage_nodes, refreshed on @full samples. Built with --enable-beegfs (default on).
BeeGFS mount directory as returned by getmntent from /proc/mounts, e.g. /mnt/beegfs. Octal escapes are decoded, so a mount path with a space shows a real space.
Placeholder for a BeeGFS read operation counter. Always reported as not present: the BeeGFS client exposes no per-operation counters and beegfs-ctl --clientstats is deliberately not queried. No data.

Bytes received on established TCP connections to this mount's BeeGFS storage servers (tcp_info bytes_received, growth summed across sockets). Per-block-device I/O statistics from /sys/block/<dev>/stat (first 11 fields). Whole devices only (no partitions); ram* and loop* devices are skipped. Rows appear every sample.
Block device name as listed in /sys/block, e.g. nvme0n1, sda or dm-0.
Read requests completed by the device (/sys/block/<dev>/stat field 1). Counter: delta / elapsed s = read IOPS.
Read requests merged with an adjacent queued request before reaching the device (/sys/block/<dev>/stat field 2). Counter: take the difference between samples and divide by elapsed seconds for a rate.
Sectors read (/sys/block/<dev>/stat field 3); always 512-byte units regardless of device sector size. Counter: delta x 512 = bytes; divide by elapsed s for read bandwidth.
Total milliseconds read requests spent waiting and being serviced (/sys/block/<dev>/stat field 4). Counter in ms: delta(rd_ticks) / delta(rd_ios) = average read latency in ms.
Write requests completed by the device (/sys/block/<dev>/stat field 5). Counter: delta / elapsed s = write IOPS.

Write requests merged with an adjacent queued request before reaching the device (/sys/block/<dev>/stat field 6). Counter: take the difference between samples and divide by elapsed seconds for a rate.
Sectors written (/sys/block/<dev>/stat field 7); always 512-byte units regardless of device sector size. Counter: delta x 512 = bytes; divide by elapsed s for write bandwidth.
Total milliseconds write requests spent waiting and being serviced (/sys/block/<dev>/stat field 8). Counter in ms: delta(wr_ticks) / delta(wr_ios) = average write latency in ms.
I/O requests issued to the device but not yet completed at sample time (/sys/block/<dev>/stat field 9). Gauge, a count; read as is.
Milliseconds the device had at least one request in flight (/sys/block/<dev>/stat field 10). Counter in ms: delta / (1000 x elapsed s) = device busy fraction (utilization).
Weighted milliseconds spent by all requests, i.e. time x requests in flight (/sys/block/<dev>/stat field 11). Counter in ms: delta / (1000 x elapsed s) = average queue depth.

Per-logical-CPU time accounting from the cpuN lines of /proc/stat (the aggregate cpu line is skipped; steal and guest are not collected). Read every sample, so rows appear in both @fast and @full records, one per online CPU.
Logical CPU number taken from the /proc/stat cpuN line, e.g. 0 for cpu0.

Time this CPU spent running user-mode code at normal priority (/proc/stat cpuN field 1, user). Counter in centiseconds (USER_HZ jiffies, 100 per second in practice); delta / (100 x elapsed s) = fraction of this CPU, or divide by the delta of all seven keys.

Time this CPU spent running user-mode code of niced (low priority) processes (/proc/stat cpuN field 2, nice). Counter in centiseconds (USER_HZ jiffies, 100 per second in practice); delta / (100 x elapsed s) = fraction of this CPU, or divide by the delta of all seven keys.

Time this CPU spent in kernel mode, excluding irq/softirq (/proc/stat cpuN field 3, system). High values suggest syscall, page fault or filesystem overhead. Counter in centiseconds (USER_HZ jiffies, 100 per second in practice); delta / (100 x elapsed s) = fraction of this CPU, or divide by the delta of all seven keys.

Time this CPU spent in the idle task (/proc/stat cpuN field 4, idle). Counter in centiseconds (USER_HZ jiffies, 100 per second in practice); delta / (100 x elapsed s) = fraction of this CPU, or divide by the delta of all seven keys.

Time this CPU was idle while I/O was outstanding (/proc/stat cpuN field 5, iowait). The kernel treats it as approximate idle time, not busy time. Counter in centiseconds (USER_HZ jiffies, 100 per second in practice); delta / (100 x elapsed s) = fraction of this CPU, or divide by the delta of all seven keys.

Time this CPU spent servicing hardware interrupts (/proc/stat cpuN field 6, irq). Counter in centiseconds (USER_HZ jiffies, 100 per second in practice); delta / (100 x elapsed s) = fraction of this CPU, or divide by the delta of all seven keys.

Time this CPU spent servicing soft interrupts such as network and block completion (/proc/stat cpuN field 7, softirq). Counter in centiseconds (USER_HZ jiffies, 100 per second in practice); delta / (100 x elapsed s) = fraction of this CPU, or divide by the delta of all seven keys.

Per-logical-CPU core counters read by direct perf_event_open on the core PMU (cpu on x86, armv8_pmuv3 on aarch64), never pinned and scaled by enabled/running time like perf stat. x86 builds fill Intel or AMD keys by runtime CPU model; the aarch64 arm backend (Grace) adds /proc/stat util and cpufreq cycle keys. Keys a CPU lacks emit -2 NOT_PRESENT.
Logical CPU index as in /proc/stat and sysfs cpuN, e.g. 0. One row per CPU; sum the rows for a host total.

CPU microseconds this CPU was busy: all non-idle, non-iowait /proc/stat time (user, nice, system, irq, softirq, steal, guest), accumulated each collect. Grace (arm backend) only; x86 rows emit -2 NOT_PRESENT. Slow-tier key (only in @full rows). delta / (1e6 x elapsed s) = busy fraction. Builds before the units fix were 100x larger.

CPU microseconds in user mode, including nice time (/proc/stat user + nice). Grace (arm backend) only; x86 rows emit -2 NOT_PRESENT. Slow-tier key (only in @full rows). delta / (1e6 x elapsed s) = user fraction of this CPU.

CPU microseconds in kernel (system) mode from /proc/stat. Grace (arm backend) only; x86 rows emit -2 NOT_PRESENT. Slow-tier key (only in @full rows). delta / (1e6 x elapsed s) = system fraction of this CPU.

CPU microseconds servicing hardware and soft interrupts (/proc/stat irq + softirq). Grace (arm backend) only; x86 rows emit -2 NOT_PRESENT. Slow-tier key (only in @full rows). delta / (1e6 x elapsed s) = interrupt fraction of this CPU.
Always 0 on Grace: nice time is folded into cpu_util_user_accum_us. x86 rows emit -2 NOT_PRESENT. Slow-tier key (only in @full rows). Kept for schema compatibility; do not use.

Grace only: core cycles of this CPU, 64-bit. Measured CPU_CYCLES (direct perf, scaled) when the cycle counter is open; otherwise an estimate of cpufreq scaling_cur_freq x busy time. x86 rows emit -2 NOT_PRESENT (use aperf). delta / elapsed s = cycles per second.

Intel only: instructions retired (perf instructions on the fixed counter), lifetime modulo 2^48. Same value as instr_retired. AMD and Grace emit -2 NOT_PRESENT. delta / elapsed s = instructions/s; divide by the cycles_unhalted_core delta for IPC.

Intel only: core clock cycles while not halted (perf cpu-cycles, fixed counter), modulo 2^48. Same value as aperf. AMD and Grace emit -2 NOT_PRESENT. delta / elapsed s = average running clock in Hz. With nmi_watchdog=1 the counter is shared, so values are scaled estimates.

Intel only: unhalted reference cycles at the nominal (TSC) rate (perf ref-cycles), modulo 2^48. Same value as mperf. AMD and Grace emit -2 NOT_PRESENT. cycles_unhalted_core delta / this delta = effective clock relative to nominal (above 1 = turbo).

Retired load instructions whose data hit the L1 data cache (event 0xd1 umask 0x01), modulo 2^48. Intel SKX/CLX/ICX/SPR/EMR/GNR only; AMD, Sierra Forest and Grace emit -2 NOT_PRESENT. On ICX/SPR/EMR/GNR data before 3.1 this key counted all loads; do not compare across that upgrade.

Retired load instructions whose data hit the L2 cache (event 0xd1 umask 0x02), modulo 2^48. Intel SKX/CLX/ICX/SPR/EMR/GNR only; AMD, Sierra Forest and Grace emit -2 NOT_PRESENT. ICX and newer emitted -10 NOT_BUILT before 3.1.

Retired load instructions whose data hit the last-level (L3) cache (event 0xd1 umask 0x04), modulo 2^48. Intel SKX/CLX/ICX/SPR/EMR/GNR only; AMD, Sierra Forest and Grace emit -2 NOT_PRESENT. ICX and newer emitted -10 NOT_BUILT before 3.1.

L1 data cache lines replaced, i.e. lines brought into L1D after a miss (event 0x51 umask 0x01), modulo 2^48. Intel SKX/CLX/ICX/SPR/EMR/GNR only; AMD, Sierra Forest and Grace emit -2 NOT_PRESENT. delta / elapsed s = L1D miss fills per second.

Retired instructions (AMD event 0xc0), modulo 2^48. AMD Milan/Genoa/Turin only; Intel, Rome and Grace emit -2 NOT_PRESENT. Shares one counter with instr_retired on AMD, so the two keys carry the same value.
Retired branch instructions (AMD event 0xc2), modulo 2^48. AMD Milan/Genoa/Turin only; Intel, Rome and Grace emit -2 NOT_PRESENT. delta / retired_instructions delta = branch fraction.

Retired mispredicted branch instructions (AMD event 0xc3), modulo 2^48. AMD Milan/Genoa/Turin only; Intel, Rome and Grace emit -2 NOT_PRESENT. delta / retired_branch_instr delta = branch misprediction rate.

Load/store unit dispatches: loads, stores and load-op-store ops dispatched (AMD event 0x29 umask 0x07), modulo 2^48. AMD Milan/Genoa/Turin only; Intel, Rome and Grace emit -2 NOT_PRESENT. A proxy for memory-instruction volume.

Instructions retired on this CPU, modulo 2^48. Intel: perf instructions (equals instr_retired_any); AMD: generic instructions event (equals retired_instructions); Grace: INST_RETIRED via direct perf. Filled on every x86 class incl. Rome and SRF. delta / elapsed s = instructions/s.

Core cycles while running, modulo 2^48 (perf cycles, not the APERF MSR). Intel/AMD: perf cpu-cycles (Intel: equals cycles_unhalted_core). Grace: measured CPU_CYCLES when open, else util x cpufreq estimate. delta / elapsed s = clock Hz; instr_retired delta / aperf delta = IPC.

Reference cycles, modulo 2^48. Intel: perf ref-cycles (equals cycles_unhalted_ref). AMD emits -2 NOT_PRESENT. Grace: equals aperf (measured CPU_CYCLES) when the cycle counter is open, else cpufreq x wall time, so aperf/mperf is not a frequency ratio on Grace.

Retired legacy key (before 3.1: AMD Data Fabric channel 0 64-byte beats despite the name). Always a sentinel now: x86 rows emit -2 NOT_PRESENT, Grace -10 NOT_BUILT. Use amd_x86_uncore_df_* chan<N> rows or arm_aarch64_imc instead.

Retired scalar double-precision FP arithmetic instructions (event 0xc7 umask 0x01), modulo 2^48; an FMA counts twice. FLOPs = count x 1. Intel SKX/CLX/ICX/SPR/EMR/GNR only; AMD, Sierra Forest and Grace emit -2 NOT_PRESENT. Sum all widths' weighted deltas / elapsed s for the FP64 FLOP rate.

Retired 512-bit packed single-precision FP arithmetic instructions (event 0xc7 umask 0x80), modulo 2^48; an FMA counts twice. FLOPs = count x 16. Intel SKX/CLX/ICX/SPR/EMR/GNR only; AMD, Sierra Forest and Grace emit -2 NOT_PRESENT. Sum all widths' weighted deltas / elapsed s for the FP32 FLOP rate.

Grace: measured floating-point operations, FP_FIXED_OPS_SPEC + FP_SCALE_OPS_SPEC (direct perf, scaled), all precisions combined, 64-bit. delta / elapsed s = FLOP/s. Excludes SVE integer ops. Always 0 before 3.1. x86 and aarch64 cores without a verified MIDR row emit -2.

Grace: SVE 8-bit integer instructions speculatively executed (ASE_SVE_INT8_SPEC, direct perf, scaled), modulo 2^48. Instructions, not FLOPs. Always 0 before 3.1. x86 and aarch64 cores without a verified MIDR row emit -2 NOT_PRESENT.

Grace: SVE 16-bit integer instructions speculatively executed (ASE_SVE_INT16_SPEC, direct perf, scaled), modulo 2^48. Instructions, not FLOPs. Always 0 before 3.1. x86 and aarch64 cores without a verified MIDR row emit -2 NOT_PRESENT.

Grace only: synthetic DRAM byte estimate, 16 bytes per active cycle where active cycles = cpufreq x wall time x CPU util (always util-based, even when cycles are measured). Not a measurement; use arm_aarch64_imc dram_cas_* for real traffic. x86 emits -2.

AMD Milan/Genoa/Turin: total retired SSE/AVX floating-point operations in FLOPs (event 0x03, all op types), 64-bit. No precision split on Zen3/Zen4 (see amd_fp_dp_ops on Turin). Intel, Rome and Grace emit -2. delta / elapsed s = FLOP/s.

AMD Turin (Zen5) only: double-precision FLOPs, packed + scalar (event 0x03 umasks 0xaf + 0x8f), 64-bit. Single precision = fp_ops_retired - amd_fp_dp_ops (bf16 lands in single). All other CPUs emit -2 NOT_PRESENT.

Nanoseconds the core events open on this CPU were enabled, summed over events, 64-bit (x86 and Grace; -2 if no core counter opened). delta pmu_running_time / delta pmu_enabled_time = share of time the events really counted; below 1 means multiplexing and scaled counts.

Nanoseconds the open core events actually ran on a hardware counter, summed over events, 64-bit. delta running / delta pmu_enabled_time = counting share (1.0 = no multiplexing); summed over CPUs for a host share.

Nanoseconds the events would run if the monitor were the only PMU user (fixed/cycle-counter events full time, general events min(1, counters / open events)). Only Intel SKX..GNR, AMD Milan/Genoa/Turin, Grace Neoverse V2; else -2. 1 - delta running / delta solo = share lost to other users (perf, nvidia-powerd).

arm (aarch64) builds only, absent from the x86 schema: FP64 (double) floating-point instructions speculatively executed, all vector widths (FP_DP_SPEC, direct perf, scaled), 64-bit. Counts instructions, not FLOPs (use arm_est_flops). -2 on a core without a verified MIDR row.

arm (aarch64) builds only, absent from the x86 schema: FP32 (single) floating-point instructions speculatively executed, all vector widths (FP_SP_SPEC, direct perf, scaled), 64-bit. Counts instructions, not FLOPs (use arm_est_flops). -2 on a core without a verified MIDR row.

arm (aarch64) builds only, absent from the x86 schema: FP16 (half) floating-point instructions speculatively executed, all vector widths (FP_HP_SPEC, direct perf, scaled), 64-bit. Counts instructions, not FLOPs (use arm_est_flops). -2 on a core without a verified MIDR row.

InfiniBand HCA port counters read from /sys/class/infiniband//ports/

/counters and hw_counters, plus sw_* counters of the attached switch port queried over MAD (needs --enable-infiniband, default, or --enable-ib-mad-dlopen, else -10 NOT_BUILT). Type is disabled when lspci/sysfs show no InfiniBand.
<hca>.<port>, e.g. mlx5_0.1. Only ports that are ACTIVE (or phys LinkUp) with link_layer InfiniBand; Omni-Path hfi1 devices are excluded (see host_opa).

Times the port saw consecutive receive buffer overruns. Read from /sys/class/infiniband//ports/

/counters/excessive_buffer_overrun_errors; unit: events. 32-bit; saturates, does not wrap. Counter: delta / elapsed s. @full rows only (default every 600 s).

Times the link error recovery process failed and the link went down; any increase means the port lost its link. Read from /sys/class/infiniband//ports/

/counters/link_downed; unit: events. 32-bit; saturates, does not wrap. Counter: delta / elapsed s.

Times the link error recovery process completed successfully (link retrained without going down). Read from /sys/class/infiniband//ports/

/counters/link_error_recovery; unit: events. 32-bit; saturates, does not wrap. Counter: delta / elapsed s.

Times local physical errors exceeded the LocalPhyErrors threshold. Read from /sys/class/infiniband//ports/

/counters/local_link_integrity_errors; unit: events. 32-bit; saturates, does not wrap. Counter: delta / elapsed s. @full rows only (default every 600 s).

Received packets discarded by partition key/constraint checks. Read from /sys/class/infiniband//ports/

/counters/port_rcv_constraint_errors; unit: packets. 32-bit; saturates, does not wrap. Counter: delta / elapsed s. @full rows only (default every 600 s).

Data received on this HCA port (InfiniBand PMA PortRcvData, counted in 4-byte words). Read from /sys/class/infiniband//ports/

/counters/port_rcv_data; unit: bytes after x4 (U=4B). 64-bit. Counter: delta / elapsed s.

Received packets containing an error and discarded. Read from /sys/class/infiniband//ports/

/counters/port_rcv_errors; unit: packets. 32-bit; saturates, does not wrap. Counter: delta / elapsed s. @full rows only (default every 600 s).

Packets received on this HCA port (PMA PortRcvPkts). Read from /sys/class/infiniband//ports/

/counters/port_rcv_packets; unit: packets. 64-bit. Counter: delta / elapsed s.

Received packets marked with EBP (bad packet) by an upstream link. Read from /sys/class/infiniband//ports/

/counters/port_rcv_remote_physical_errors; unit: packets. 32-bit; saturates, does not wrap. Counter: delta / elapsed s. @full rows only (default every 600 s).

Received packets discarded that could not be relayed; mainly a switch-port counter. Read from /sys/class/infiniband//ports/

/counters/port_rcv_switch_relay_errors; unit: packets. 32-bit; saturates, does not wrap. Counter: delta / elapsed s. @full rows only (default every 600 s).

Outbound packets not transmitted by partition/constraint checks. Read from /sys/class/infiniband//ports/

/counters/port_xmit_constraint_errors; unit: packets. 32-bit; saturates, does not wrap. Counter: delta / elapsed s. @full rows only (default every 600 s).

Data transmitted on this HCA port (PMA PortXmitData, counted in 4-byte words). Read from /sys/class/infiniband//ports/

/counters/port_xmit_data; unit: bytes after x4 (U=4B). 64-bit. Counter: delta / elapsed s.

Outbound packets discarded because the port was down or congested. Read from /sys/class/infiniband//ports/

/counters/port_xmit_discards; unit: packets. 32-bit; saturates, does not wrap. Counter: delta / elapsed s.

Packets transmitted on this HCA port (PMA PortXmitPkts). Read from /sys/class/infiniband//ports/

/counters/port_xmit_packets; unit: packets. 64-bit. Counter: delta / elapsed s.

Time the port had data to send but could not (no flow-control credits or lost arbitration); a congestion indicator. Read from /sys/class/infiniband//ports/

/counters/port_xmit_wait. Schema unit ms (W=32); the IB PMA counts this in link clock ticks, so treat scale as relative. Counter: delta / elapsed s.

Minor link errors detected on the physical lanes (PMA SymbolErrorCounter); steady rise suggests a bad cable/optic. Read from /sys/class/infiniband//ports/

/counters/symbol_error; unit: errors. 32-bit; saturates, does not wrap. Counter: delta / elapsed s. @full rows only (default every 600 s).

Bytes the host received, measured at the switch port it is cabled to. Switch-port PMA extended PortXmitData via MAD, swapped to host view; unit: bytes after x4 (U=4B). Needs --enable-infiniband (default) or --enable-ib-mad-dlopen, else sentinel -10 NOT_BUILT; -2 if the MAD port cannot be opened, -9 during failure backoff. Counter: delta/elapsed s.

Packets the host received, measured at the switch port it is cabled to. Switch-port PMA extended PortXmitPkts via MAD, swapped to host view; unit: packets. Needs --enable-infiniband (default) or --enable-ib-mad-dlopen, else sentinel -10 NOT_BUILT; -2 if the MAD port cannot be opened, -9 during failure backoff. Counter: delta/elapsed s.

Bytes the host sent, measured at the switch port it is cabled to. Switch-port PMA extended PortRcvData via MAD, swapped to host view; unit: bytes after x4 (U=4B). Needs --enable-infiniband (default) or --enable-ib-mad-dlopen, else sentinel -10 NOT_BUILT; -2 if the MAD port cannot be opened, -9 during failure backoff. Counter: delta/elapsed s.

Packets the host sent, measured at the switch port it is cabled to. Switch-port PMA extended PortRcvPkts via MAD, swapped to host view; unit: packets. Needs --enable-infiniband (default) or --enable-ib-mad-dlopen, else sentinel -10 NOT_BUILT; -2 if the MAD port cannot be opened, -9 during failure backoff. Counter: delta/elapsed s.

Lustre LNet traffic counters for the whole node, read positionally from /proc/sys/lnet/stats each sample. Always built (not gated by --enable-lustre); keys carry error sentinels if the file is missing. Allocation and drop/error keys are in @full rows only.
Always - (one node-wide row, no device).

LNet message descriptors currently allocated (Lustre reports a level; the schema flags it E). Read positionally from /proc/sys/lnet/stats (Lustre LNet), field 1; unit: messages. Treat as read; differencing gives the change in level. @full rows only (default every 600 s).

High-water mark of allocated LNet message descriptors (a level in Lustre; schema flags it E). Read positionally from /proc/sys/lnet/stats (Lustre LNet), field 2; unit: messages. Treat as read; differencing gives the change in level. @full rows only (default every 600 s).
LNet errors counted by Lustre. Read positionally from /proc/sys/lnet/stats (Lustre LNet), field 3; unit: events. Counter: delta / elapsed s. @full rows only (default every 600 s).
LNet messages sent by this node (send_count). Read positionally from /proc/sys/lnet/stats (Lustre LNet), field 4; unit: messages. Counter: delta / elapsed s.
LNet messages received by this node (recv_count). Read positionally from /proc/sys/lnet/stats (Lustre LNet), field 5; unit: messages. Counter: delta / elapsed s.
LNet messages forwarded by this node acting as an LNet router (route_count). Read positionally from /proc/sys/lnet/stats (Lustre LNet), field 6; unit: messages. Counter: delta / elapsed s.
LNet messages dropped (drop_count). Read positionally from /proc/sys/lnet/stats (Lustre LNet), field 7; unit: messages. Counter: delta / elapsed s. @full rows only (default every 600 s).
LNet payload bytes sent (send_length). Read positionally from /proc/sys/lnet/stats (Lustre LNet), field 8; unit: bytes. Counter: delta / elapsed s.
LNet payload bytes received (recv_length). Read positionally from /proc/sys/lnet/stats (Lustre LNet), field 9; unit: bytes. Counter: delta / elapsed s.
LNet payload bytes forwarded as a router (route_length). Read positionally from /proc/sys/lnet/stats (Lustre LNet), field 10; unit: bytes. Counter: delta / elapsed s.
LNet payload bytes dropped (drop_length). Read positionally from /proc/sys/lnet/stats (Lustre LNet), field 11; unit: bytes. Counter: delta / elapsed s. @full rows only (default every 600 s).

Per-NUMA-node memory usage from /sys/devices/system/node/nodeN/meminfo (Node N lines, mapped to snake_case keys). Fast keys appear in every row; keys marked slow only in @full rows. Sum across nodes for a host total.
NUMA node number from the /sys/devices/system/node/nodeN directory name, e.g. 0 for node0.
Total usable RAM on this NUMA node (node meminfo MemTotal). Gauge in KiB; read as is.
Completely unused RAM on this NUMA node (node meminfo MemFree); does not count reclaimable page cache. Gauge in KiB; read as is.
RAM in use on this NUMA node as reported by the kernel (node meminfo MemUsed, i.e. MemTotal - MemFree), so it includes page cache and slab. Gauge in KiB; read as is.
Memory on this node on the active LRU lists, i.e. recently used and unlikely to be reclaimed soon (node meminfo Active). Gauge in KiB; read as is.
Memory on this node on the inactive LRU lists, the first candidates for reclaim (node meminfo Inactive). Gauge in KiB; read as is. Slow key: @full rows only.
Page cache on this node modified but not yet written back to storage (node meminfo Dirty). Gauge in KiB; read as is. Slow key: @full rows only.
Page cache on this node currently being written back to storage (node meminfo Writeback). Gauge in KiB; read as is. Slow key: @full rows only.
File-backed page cache on this node (node meminfo FilePages); also includes tmpfs and /dev/shm files, so in-memory files show up here. Gauge in KiB; read as is.
File pages on this node mapped into process address spaces, e.g. executables, libraries, mmap'd files (node meminfo Mapped). Gauge in KiB; read as is. Slow key: @full rows only.
Anonymous (non-file-backed) memory on this node, i.e. process heap and stack (node meminfo AnonPages). Gauge in KiB; read as is. Slow key: @full rows only.
Memory on this node used for page tables (node meminfo PageTables); grows with large mappings and many processes. Gauge in KiB; read as is. Slow key: @full rows only.
NFS pages sent to the server but not yet committed to stable storage (node meminfo NFS_Unstable); always 0 or absent on newer kernels. Gauge in KiB; read as is. Slow key: @full rows only.
Memory on this node used for block-device bounce buffers (node meminfo Bounce). Gauge in KiB; read as is. Slow key: @full rows only.
Kernel slab allocator memory on this node, e.g. dentry and inode caches (node meminfo Slab). Gauge in KiB; read as is.
Anonymous memory on this node backed by transparent huge pages (node meminfo AnonHugePages). Gauge in KiB; read as is. Slow key: @full rows only.
Number of pre-allocated (hugetlbfs) huge pages of the default size on this node (node meminfo HugePages_Total). Gauge, a page count not bytes; read as is. Slow key: @full rows only.
Number of pre-allocated (hugetlbfs) huge pages of the default size on this node not yet used (node meminfo HugePages_Free). Gauge, a page count not bytes; read as is. Slow key: @full rows only.

Per-job cgroup v2 memory from the Slurm job scope (slurmstepd.scope/<token> under /sys/fs/cgroup, found from a job process). Only in shared-node builds (--enable-shared-node-multi-jid): one row per running job, omitted if its cgroup cannot be read. Kernel bytes are divided by 1024.
j:<jobid> for the Slurm job the cgroup belongs to, e.g. j:1234567.
Total memory charged to the job cgroup, including page cache and kernel memory (cgroup v2 memory.current, bytes / 1024). Gauge in KiB; read as is.
Highest memory.current seen for the job cgroup since it was created (cgroup v2 memory.peak, bytes / 1024). Gauge in KiB; read as is. Not present when the kernel has no memory.peak file.
Anonymous memory (heap, stack, anonymous mmap) charged to the job (cgroup v2 memory.stat anon, bytes / 1024). Gauge in KiB; read as is. Not present if memory.stat lacks the field.
File-backed memory charged to the job, i.e. page cache including tmpfs and shared memory (cgroup v2 memory.stat file, bytes / 1024). Gauge in KiB; read as is.
File-backed memory mapped into the job's processes via mmap (cgroup v2 memory.stat file_mapped, bytes / 1024). Gauge in KiB; read as is.
Job page cache modified but not yet written back (cgroup v2 memory.stat file_dirty, bytes / 1024). Gauge in KiB; read as is.
Job page cache currently being written back to storage (cgroup v2 memory.stat file_writeback, bytes / 1024). Gauge in KiB; read as is.
Memory used for page tables of the job's processes (cgroup v2 memory.stat pagetables, bytes / 1024). Gauge in KiB; read as is.

Per-interface network statistics from the Linux kernel, read from /sys/class/net/<if>/statistics/<key> each sample. One row per interface whose /sys/class/net/<if>/flags has IFF_UP; the interface list is cached and rebuilt every 32 samples. Always built; error/drop keys are in @full rows only.
Network interface name as listed in /sys/class/net, any interface that is up, including lo and IPoIB, e.g. eth0, ib0.

Ethernet collisions seen on this interface (mostly zero on modern full-duplex links). Read from /sys/class/net/<if>/statistics/collisions; unit: count. Counter: delta / elapsed s. @full rows only (default every 600 s).
Multicast packets received on this interface. Read from /sys/class/net/<if>/statistics/multicast; unit: packets. Counter: delta / elapsed s.
Bytes received on this interface, as counted by the driver. Read from /sys/class/net/<if>/statistics/rx_bytes; unit: bytes. Counter: delta / elapsed s.

Compressed packets received (meaningful only for drivers that do compression, e.g. PPP/SLIP; normally 0). Read from /sys/class/net/<if>/statistics/rx_compressed; unit: packets. Counter: delta / elapsed s.

Received frames dropped for a bad CRC/FCS, often a sign of a bad cable, optic or port. Read from /sys/class/net/<if>/statistics/rx_crc_errors; unit: packets. Counter: delta / elapsed s. @full rows only (default every 600 s).

Received packets dropped by the kernel or driver before delivery (e.g. no buffer, unknown protocol, filtered). Read from /sys/class/net/<if>/statistics/rx_dropped; unit: packets. Counter: delta / elapsed s. @full rows only (default every 600 s).

Total receive errors reported by the driver (the sum of the more specific rx_*_errors where supported). Read from /sys/class/net/<if>/statistics/rx_errors; unit: packets. Counter: delta / elapsed s. @full rows only (default every 600 s).

Receive FIFO/ring overflow errors reported by the driver (host did not drain the receive ring fast enough). Read from /sys/class/net/<if>/statistics/rx_fifo_errors; unit: packets. Counter: delta / elapsed s. @full rows only (default every 600 s).
Received frames with alignment/framing errors. Read from /sys/class/net/<if>/statistics/rx_frame_errors; unit: packets. Counter: delta / elapsed s. @full rows only (default every 600 s).

Received frames dropped for an invalid length (too short or too long). Read from /sys/class/net/<if>/statistics/rx_length_errors; unit: packets. Counter: delta / elapsed s. @full rows only (default every 600 s).

Packets the NIC missed because it had no buffer space (driver-reported). Read from /sys/class/net/<if>/statistics/rx_missed_errors; unit: packets. Counter: delta / elapsed s. @full rows only (default every 600 s).

Receiver overrun errors: packets lost because the NIC ring or buffer overflowed. Read from /sys/class/net/<if>/statistics/rx_over_errors; unit: packets. Counter: delta / elapsed s. @full rows only (default every 600 s).
Packets received on this interface. Read from /sys/class/net/<if>/statistics/rx_packets; unit: packets. Counter: delta / elapsed s.

Transmits aborted by the hardware (e.g. too many collisions or link errors). Read from /sys/class/net/<if>/statistics/tx_aborted_errors; unit: packets. Counter: delta / elapsed s. @full rows only (default every 600 s).
Bytes transmitted on this interface, as counted by the driver. Read from /sys/class/net/<if>/statistics/tx_bytes; unit: bytes. Counter: delta / elapsed s.

Transmit errors due to loss of carrier (link down or flapping during send). Read from /sys/class/net/<if>/statistics/tx_carrier_errors; unit: packets. Counter: delta / elapsed s. @full rows only (default every 600 s).
Compressed packets transmitted (only for drivers that do compression; normally 0). Read from /sys/class/net/<if>/statistics/tx_compressed; unit: packets. Counter: delta / elapsed s.

Transmit packets dropped before reaching the wire (e.g. queue full, no route in driver). Read from /sys/class/net/<if>/statistics/tx_dropped; unit: packets. Counter: delta / elapsed s. @full rows only (default every 600 s).
Total transmit errors reported by the driver. Read from /sys/class/net/<if>/statistics/tx_errors; unit: packets. Counter: delta / elapsed s. @full rows only (default every 600 s).

Transmit FIFO underrun/overflow errors reported by the driver. Read from /sys/class/net/<if>/statistics/tx_fifo_errors; unit: packets. Counter: delta / elapsed s. @full rows only (default every 600 s).

Transmit heartbeat (SQE test) errors; legacy Ethernet, normally 0. Read from /sys/class/net/<if>/statistics/tx_heartbeat_errors; unit: packets. Counter: delta / elapsed s. @full rows only (default every 600 s).
Packets transmitted on this interface. Read from /sys/class/net/<if>/statistics/tx_packets; unit: packets. Counter: delta / elapsed s.

Late-collision (transmit window) errors; legacy half-duplex Ethernet, normally 0. Read from /sys/class/net/<if>/statistics/tx_window_errors; unit: packets. Counter: delta / elapsed s. @full rows only (default every 600 s).

NFS client per-mount statistics read from /proc/self/mountstats (events:, bytes:, xprt: and READ/WRITE per-op lines, parsed by position). Rows appear only for mounts with fstype nfs or nfs4 and statvers 1.0 or 1.1; always built.
NFS mount point as printed in /proc/self/mountstats, kernel-escaped, e.g. /home1 (a space appears as \040).

Times NFS operations were delayed because the server asked the client to retry later (JUKEBOX/NFS4ERR_DELAY). Field 25 of the 'events:' line of /proc/self/mountstats; unit: events. Counter: delta / elapsed s.
Bytes applications read through normal (buffered, page cache) read calls on this mount. Field 1 from the 'bytes:' line of /proc/self/mountstats; unit: bytes. Counter: delta / elapsed s.
Bytes applications wrote through normal (buffered) write calls on this mount. Field 2 from the 'bytes:' line of /proc/self/mountstats; unit: bytes. Counter: delta / elapsed s.
Bytes read with O_DIRECT on this mount. Field 3 from the 'bytes:' line of /proc/self/mountstats; unit: bytes. Counter: delta / elapsed s.
Bytes written with O_DIRECT on this mount. Field 4 from the 'bytes:' line of /proc/self/mountstats; unit: bytes. Counter: delta / elapsed s.
Bytes actually read from the NFS server (normal reads that missed cache plus direct reads). Field 5 from the 'bytes:' line of /proc/self/mountstats; unit: bytes. Counter: delta / elapsed s.
Bytes actually written to the NFS server. Field 6 from the 'bytes:' line of /proc/self/mountstats; unit: bytes. Counter: delta / elapsed s.

RPC replies whose transaction ID matched no outstanding request (late or duplicate replies). Read by position from the 'xprt:' line of /proc/self/mountstats (after 4 udp or 7 tcp/rdma fields); unit: replies. Counter: delta / elapsed s. @full rows only (default every 600 s).

Running sum of requests in flight, added at each RPC send. Read by position from the 'xprt:' line of /proc/self/mountstats (after 4 udp or 7 tcp/rdma fields). Delta / delta sends (not collected) = mean requests in flight. Counter: delta / elapsed s. @full rows only (default every 600 s).

Running sum of backlog queue length, added at each RPC send; growth means requests waited for a slot. Read by position from the 'xprt:' line of /proc/self/mountstats (after 4 udp or 7 tcp/rdma fields). Delta / delta sends (not collected) = mean backlog. Counter: delta / elapsed s. @full rows only (default every 600 s).
READ RPC operations issued on this mount. Field 1 of the 'READ:' per-op line in /proc/self/mountstats; unit: operations. Counter: delta / elapsed s.

Major timeouts on READ RPCs (server did not answer in time; often hangs or retransmits). Field 3 of the 'READ:' per-op line in /proc/self/mountstats; unit: timeouts. Counter: delta / elapsed s. @full rows only (default every 600 s).

Cumulative time READ RPCs waited in the client queue before being sent. Divide delta by delta read_ops for average queue ms per op. Field 6 of the 'READ:' per-op line in /proc/self/mountstats; unit: ms (U=ms). Counter: delta / elapsed s.

Cumulative round-trip time of READ RPCs (send to reply). Divide delta by delta read_ops for average latency per op. Field 7 of the 'READ:' per-op line in /proc/self/mountstats; unit: ms (U=ms). Counter: delta / elapsed s.
WRITE RPC operations issued on this mount. Field 1 of the 'WRITE:' per-op line in /proc/self/mountstats; unit: operations. Counter: delta / elapsed s.

Major timeouts on WRITE RPCs (server did not answer in time; often hangs or retransmits). Field 3 of the 'WRITE:' per-op line in /proc/self/mountstats; unit: timeouts. Counter: delta / elapsed s. @full rows only (default every 600 s).

Cumulative time WRITE RPCs waited in the client queue before being sent. Divide delta by delta write_ops for average queue ms per op. Field 6 of the 'WRITE:' per-op line in /proc/self/mountstats; unit: ms (U=ms). Counter: delta / elapsed s.

Cumulative round-trip time of WRITE RPCs (send to reply). Divide delta by delta write_ops for average latency per op. Field 7 of the 'WRITE:' per-op line in /proc/self/mountstats; unit: ms (U=ms). Counter: delta / elapsed s.

Per-NUMA-node page allocation placement counters from /sys/devices/system/node/nodeN/numastat. All keys are page counts since boot; fast keys appear in every row, interleave_hit and local_node only in @full rows.
NUMA node number from the /sys/devices/system/node/nodeN directory name, e.g. 0 for node0.
Pages allocated on this node that were intended for this node (numastat numa_hit). Counter: take the difference between samples and divide by elapsed seconds for a rate.

Pages allocated on this node although another node was preferred, because the preferred node was short of memory (numastat numa_miss). Counter: take the difference between samples and divide by elapsed seconds for a rate.

Pages intended for this node that were allocated on another node instead (numastat numa_foreign); the mirror of numa_miss. Counter: take the difference between samples and divide by elapsed seconds for a rate.

Interleave-policy pages that were allocated on this node as intended (numastat interleave_hit). Counter: take the difference between samples and divide by elapsed seconds for a rate. Slow key: @full rows only.

Pages allocated on this node while the allocating process ran on this node (numastat local_node). Counter: take the difference between samples and divide by elapsed seconds for a rate. Slow key: @full rows only.

Pages allocated on this node while the allocating process ran on another node (numastat other_node); a sign of remote memory placement. Counter: take the difference between samples and divide by elapsed seconds for a rate.

Omni-Path/Cornelis HFI port counters, queried as STL PMA DataPortCounters over MAD when built with --enable-opa or --enable-opa-mad-dlopen; otherwise the traffic keys fall back to sysfs /sys/class/infiniband/hfi1_*/ports/

/counters or hw_counters and STL-only keys carry sentinels. Disabled when no hfi1 device is found.
<hfi>/<port> for hfi1 devices in /sys/class/infiniband with a collectible port, e.g. hfi1_0/1.

Data transmitted by this OPA HFI port. Source: STL PMA DataPortCounters port_xmit_data via MAD; without MAD, sysfs ports/

/counters/port_xmit_data or hw_counters/TxWords. No U= in schema: raw source units, not converted. Counter: delta/elapsed s.

Data received by this OPA HFI port. Source: STL PMA DataPortCounters port_rcv_data via MAD; without MAD, sysfs ports/

/counters/port_rcv_data or hw_counters/RxWords. No U= in schema: raw source units, not converted. Counter: delta/elapsed s.

Packets transmitted by this OPA HFI port. Source: STL PMA DataPortCounters port_xmit_pkts via MAD; without MAD, sysfs ports/

/counters/port_xmit_packets or hw_counters/TxPkt. No U= in schema: raw source units, not converted. Counter: delta/elapsed s.

Packets received by this OPA HFI port. Source: STL PMA DataPortCounters port_rcv_pkts via MAD; without MAD, sysfs ports/

/counters/port_rcv_packets or hw_counters/RxPkt. No U= in schema: raw source units, not converted. Counter: delta/elapsed s.

Multicast packets transmitted by this HFI port. Source: STL PMA DataPortCounters port_multicast_xmit_pkts via MAD; without MAD, sysfs ports/

/counters/multicast_xmit_packets. No U= in schema: raw source units, not converted. Counter: delta/elapsed s.

Multicast packets received by this HFI port. Source: STL PMA DataPortCounters port_multicast_rcv_pkts via MAD; without MAD, sysfs ports/

/counters/multicast_rcv_packets. No U= in schema: raw source units, not converted. Counter: delta/elapsed s.

Time the port had data queued but could not send (credit/arbitration wait); congestion indicator, raw STL/sysfs units. Source: STL PMA DataPortCounters port_xmit_wait via MAD; without MAD, sysfs ports/

/counters/port_xmit_wait or hw_counters/TxWait. No U= in schema: raw source units, not converted. Counter: delta/elapsed s.

STL SwPortCongestion: congestion events counted at the port (as reported by the PMA). Source: STL PMA DataPortCounters sw_port_congestion via MAD only (no sysfs fallback). Needs --enable-opa or --enable-opa-mad-dlopen; else -10 NOT_BUILT (-2 lib missing, -9 backoff, -7 MAD error). Counter: delta/elapsed s.

Received packets marked with FECN (forward explicit congestion notification). Source: STL PMA DataPortCounters port_rcv_fecn via MAD only (no sysfs fallback). Needs --enable-opa or --enable-opa-mad-dlopen; else -10 NOT_BUILT (-2 lib missing, -9 backoff, -7 MAD error). Counter: delta/elapsed s.

Received packets marked with BECN (backward explicit congestion notification). Source: STL PMA DataPortCounters port_rcv_becn via MAD only (no sysfs fallback). Needs --enable-opa or --enable-opa-mad-dlopen; else -10 NOT_BUILT (-2 lib missing, -9 backoff, -7 MAD error). Counter: delta/elapsed s.

STL PortXmitTimeCong: time the port spent in a congested transmit state. Source: STL PMA DataPortCounters port_xmit_time_cong via MAD only (no sysfs fallback). Needs --enable-opa or --enable-opa-mad-dlopen; else -10 NOT_BUILT (-2 lib missing, -9 backoff, -7 MAD error). Counter: delta/elapsed s.

STL PortXmitWastedBW: transmit bandwidth wasted (e.g. idle while packets pending). Source: STL PMA DataPortCounters port_xmit_wasted_bw via MAD only (no sysfs fallback). Needs --enable-opa or --enable-opa-mad-dlopen; else -10 NOT_BUILT (-2 lib missing, -9 backoff, -7 MAD error). Counter: delta/elapsed s.

STL PortXmitWaitData: transmit wait time while data was pending. Source: STL PMA DataPortCounters port_xmit_wait_data via MAD only (no sysfs fallback). Needs --enable-opa or --enable-opa-mad-dlopen; else -10 NOT_BUILT (-2 lib missing, -9 backoff, -7 MAD error). Counter: delta/elapsed s.

STL PortRcvBubble: receive bubbles (idle gaps inside incoming packets). Source: STL PMA DataPortCounters port_rcv_bubble via MAD only (no sysfs fallback). Needs --enable-opa or --enable-opa-mad-dlopen; else -10 NOT_BUILT (-2 lib missing, -9 backoff, -7 MAD error). Counter: delta/elapsed s.

STL PortMarkFECN: packets this port marked with FECN due to congestion. Source: STL PMA DataPortCounters port_mark_fecn via MAD only (no sysfs fallback). Needs --enable-opa or --enable-opa-mad-dlopen; else -10 NOT_BUILT (-2 lib missing, -9 backoff, -7 MAD error). Counter: delta/elapsed s.

STL PortErrorCounterSummary: sum of all port error counters; any increase means some error counter moved. Source: STL PMA DataPortCounters port_error_counter_summary via MAD only (no sysfs fallback). Needs --enable-opa or --enable-opa-mad-dlopen; else -10 NOT_BUILT (-2 lib missing, -9 backoff, -7 MAD error). Counter: delta/elapsed s.

Per-socket power gauges from ACPI power meters (acpi_power_meter hwmon, power1_average microwatts rounded to whole watts) labelled '<Name> Power Socket <N>'. Built on every arch but enabled only where such meters exist (NVIDIA Grace: GH200, GB200, Grace/Grace); x86 nodes disable it.
Socket index N taken from the meter label 'Power Socket N', e.g. 0. Sum rows by dev for node totals.

CPU core rail power of this socket in watts (ACPI 'CPU Power Socket N'), instantaneous meter average. Already included in socket_power_w; do not add them. -2 NOT_PRESENT if this meter is missing, -3 READ_FAILED on a failed read.

Whole-socket power in watts (ACPI 'Grace Power Socket N'), including cpu_power_w and sysio_power_w. Measured about 88-91 W on GB200 and 67-76 W on Grace/Grace. Sum over sockets for node CPU-side power. -2 NOT_PRESENT if this meter is missing, -3 READ_FAILED on a failed read.

SoC / IO rail power of this socket in watts (ACPI 'SysIO Power Socket N'), about 0.6 W on GH200 and 6 W on GB200. Already inside socket_power_w. -2 NOT_PRESENT if this meter is missing, -3 READ_FAILED on a failed read.

Whole GH200 module power in watts (ACPI 'Module Power Socket N'), including the GPU; about 130 W. GH200 only; elsewhere the meter is absent (sentinel) or 0. Do not add socket or GPU power to it. -2 NOT_PRESENT if this meter is missing, -3 READ_FAILED on a failed read.

Per-process memory and thread counts from /proc/<pid>/status. Processes owned by root, by postfix/rpc/rpcuser/dbus/daemon/ntp, or named bash, sshd, systemd etc. are skipped; rows are dropped once the process exits. If a scan takes >=10 s, collection pauses 120 s (HPCPERFSTATS_PROC_WARN_SEC / _COOLDOWN_SEC).
name/pid/cpus_allowed_list/mems_allowed_list from /proc/<pid>/status, e.g. python3/12345/0-55/0-1. The name is the raw comm (up to 15 chars) and may contain / or spaces, so split from the right.
Real user id of the process: first number of the Uid: line in /proc/<pid>/status. Gauge (an identifier, not a quantity); map to a user name with the passwd database. Slow key: @full rows only.
Peak virtual address space size of the process (/proc/<pid>/status VmPeak). Gauge in KiB; read as is. Virtual size, not physical memory.
Current virtual address space size of the process (/proc/<pid>/status VmSize). Gauge in KiB; read as is. Virtual size, often far above physical use.
Locked (mlock'd, unswappable) memory of the process (/proc/<pid>/status VmLck). Gauge in KiB; read as is. Slow key: @full rows only.
Peak resident set size (high water mark of physical memory) of the process (/proc/<pid>/status VmHWM). Gauge in KiB; read as is. Slow key: @full rows only.
Current resident set size, physical memory in use by the process including shared pages (/proc/<pid>/status VmRSS). Gauge in KiB; read as is. Summing across processes double-counts shared memory.
Size of the process data segment plus private anonymous mappings such as heap (/proc/<pid>/status VmData). Gauge in KiB; read as is. Virtual size, not necessarily resident.
Size of the main thread stack of the process (/proc/<pid>/status VmStk). Gauge in KiB; read as is.
Size of the executable text (code) segment of the process (/proc/<pid>/status VmExe). Gauge in KiB; read as is.
Size of shared library code mapped by the process (/proc/<pid>/status VmLib). Gauge in KiB; read as is.
Memory used by the page tables of the process (/proc/<pid>/status VmPTE). Gauge in KiB; read as is. Slow key: @full rows only.
Anonymous memory of the process that is swapped out (/proc/<pid>/status VmSwap). Gauge in KiB; read as is. Nonzero means the process is under memory pressure.
Number of threads in the process (/proc/<pid>/status Threads). Gauge, a count; read as is. Compare with the CPU count in cpus_allowed_list for oversubscription.

Host-wide scheduler and process activity from /proc/stat (ctxt, processes) and /proc/loadavg (load averages, runnable and total threads). Rows appear every sample; the load averages only in @full rows.
Always - (one row for the whole host).
Context switches across all CPUs since boot (/proc/stat ctxt). Counter: take the difference between samples and divide by elapsed seconds for a rate.
Processes and threads created (forks/clones) since boot (/proc/stat processes). Counter: take the difference between samples and divide by elapsed seconds for a rate.
1-minute load average from /proc/loadavg field 1, stored x100 as an integer (e.g. 1234 = load 12.34). Gauge: divide by 100 and compare with the CPU count. Slow key: @full rows only.
5-minute load average from /proc/loadavg field 2, stored x100 as an integer (e.g. 1234 = load 12.34). Gauge: divide by 100 and compare with the CPU count. Slow key: @full rows only.
15-minute load average from /proc/loadavg field 3, stored x100 as an integer (e.g. 1234 = load 12.34). Gauge: divide by 100 and compare with the CPU count. Slow key: @full rows only.
Currently runnable threads (numerator of /proc/loadavg field 4, e.g. 17 in 17/900). Gauge, a count; read as is.
Total threads (kernel scheduling entities) that exist on the host (denominator of /proc/loadavg field 4, e.g. 900 in 17/900). Gauge, a count; read as is.

Host-level theoretical peaks for roofline analysis, detected once (cpufreq and cpuinfo flags, EDAC DIMM speeds, CPU/GPU identity tables, NVML / nvidia-smi, DRM sysfs) and cached. First emitted with the header (schema/rotation) collect; later rows repeat the cached values. All archs; 0 when unknown.
Always '-' (one node-wide row).

Theoretical CPU FP64 peak in FLOP/s: sum over logical CPUs of base (else max) clock x FP64 FLOPs per cycle from cpuinfo flags (AVX-512+FMA 32, AVX2+FMA 16, SVE 8, NEON/SSE2 4). Counts every logical CPU, so SMT siblings inflate it.
CPU DRAM peak bandwidth in B/s: sum of EDAC DIMM speeds (MT/s x 8 bytes), else a CPU identity table (e.g. Grace 512e9, SPR 614.4e9, Genoa 921.6e9). cpu_peak_source says which path was used. Gauge.
CPU on-package HBM peak bandwidth in B/s, from EDAC HBM entries or the identity table (SPR Max 3.2768e12). 0 on nodes without CPU HBM. Added with peak_calc_version 2.

Sum over the node's GPUs of FP64 peak FLOP/s: NVML SM count x SM clock x FP64 ratio from compute capability, else nvidia-smi plus the SM table, or AMD rocminfo. 0 on GPU-less nodes. gpu_peak_source says which path.
Sum over GPUs of memory peak bandwidth in B/s: DRM sysfs memory attributes, else allowlisted HBM/GDDR values by GPU name (e.g. H100 3.35e12, GB200 8e12 each). 0 on GPU-less nodes.
Sum over GPUs of CPU-GPU link peak bandwidth in B/s: PCIe speed x width from sysfs, replaced by NVLink-C2C (900e9 per GH200) when that is larger. 0 on GPU-less nodes.
Enum for how the CPU peaks were found: 0 fail-open (unknown), 1 probed (EDAC / procfs), 2 identity table (Grace part 0xd4f, or x86/AMD CPUID DRAM/HBM allowlist).
Enum for how the GPU peaks were found: 0 fail-open (unknown / zero), 1 probed DRM sysfs, 2 NVML, 3 nvidia-smi, 4 GPU identity table (allowlisted HBM peak by name).
Version of the peak calculation, currently 2 (adds cpu_peak_hbm_bw_bytes_per_s and the EDAC HBM/DDR split). Compare peak values only within one version.
Host-wide System V shared memory usage, summed over all segments listed in /proc/sysvipc/shm (header line skipped). Rows appear every sample. POSIX shared memory in /dev/shm is not counted here.
Always - (one row for the whole host).
Total size of all System V shared memory segments: sum of the size column of /proc/sysvipc/shm. Gauge in bytes; read as is. This is the allocated segment size, not necessarily resident memory.
Number of System V shared memory segments: count of data lines in /proc/sysvipc/shm. Gauge, a count; read as is.

Space and inode usage of /tmp, only when /proc/mounts shows /tmp mounted as tmpfs (other tmpfs mounts are ignored), read with statfs(). Since tmpfs lives in RAM, usage here consumes node memory. All keys are slow: @full rows only.
The mount point, always /tmp (no row when /tmp is not a tmpfs).
Bytes used in the /tmp tmpfs: statfs f_frsize x (f_blocks - f_bfree). Gauge in bytes; read as is.
Bytes still available to unprivileged users in the /tmp tmpfs: statfs f_frsize x f_bavail. Gauge in bytes; read as is.
Inodes (files and directories) used in the /tmp tmpfs: statfs f_files - f_ffree. Gauge, a count; read as is.
Host-wide VFS object usage from /proc/sys/fs/dentry-state, file-nr and inode-state. All keys are slow, so rows appear only in @full records.
Always - (one row for the whole host).
Directory cache entries in use: nr_dentry minus nr_unused from /proc/sys/fs/dentry-state. Gauge, a count; read as is.

Open file handles allocated host-wide: first field of /proc/sys/fs/file-nr (the free field is always 0 since Linux 2.6, so allocated equals used). Gauge, a count; compare with the third field (max) of file-nr.
In-memory inodes in use: nr_inodes minus nr_free_inodes from /proc/sys/fs/inode-state. Gauge, a count; read as is.

Host-wide virtual memory activity from /proc/vmstat, read by field name. All keys are slow, so rows appear only in @full records (every sample_freq_slow). Names the running kernel does not provide are recorded as not present.
Always - (one row for the whole host).
Number of transparent huge pages currently backing anonymous memory (/proc/vmstat nr_anon_transparent_hugepages). Gauge, a count of huge pages not bytes; read as is.
Data read in from block devices (/proc/vmstat pgpgin; the kernel reports it in KiB). Counter in KiB: delta / elapsed s = KiB/s read.
Data written out to block devices (/proc/vmstat pgpgout; the kernel reports it in KiB). Counter in KiB: delta / elapsed s = KiB/s written.
Pages swapped in from swap space (/proc/vmstat pswpin). Nonzero rates mean memory pressure. Counter: take the difference between samples and divide by elapsed seconds for a rate.
Pages swapped out to swap space (/proc/vmstat pswpout). Nonzero rates mean memory pressure. Counter: take the difference between samples and divide by elapsed seconds for a rate.
Page allocations from the Normal memory zone (/proc/vmstat pgalloc_normal); excludes DMA/DMA32/Movable zones. Counter: take the difference between samples and divide by elapsed seconds for a rate.
Pages freed (/proc/vmstat pgfree). Counter: take the difference between samples and divide by elapsed seconds for a rate.
Pages moved from the inactive to the active LRU list (/proc/vmstat pgactivate). Counter: take the difference between samples and divide by elapsed seconds for a rate.
Pages moved from the active to the inactive LRU list (/proc/vmstat pgdeactivate). Counter: take the difference between samples and divide by elapsed seconds for a rate.
Page faults of all kinds, minor and major (/proc/vmstat pgfault). Counter: take the difference between samples and divide by elapsed seconds for a rate.
Major page faults, i.e. faults that needed I/O to bring the page in (/proc/vmstat pgmajfault). Counter: take the difference between samples and divide by elapsed seconds for a rate.

Pages scanned on the active list of the Normal zone during reclaim (/proc/vmstat pgrefill_normal). Older per-zone kernel name; newer kernels renamed or removed it, and then the value is recorded as not present rather than 0. Counter: delta / elapsed s.

Pages reclaimed from the Normal zone (/proc/vmstat pgsteal_normal). Older per-zone kernel name; newer kernels renamed or removed it, and then the value is recorded as not present rather than 0. Counter: delta / elapsed s.

Pages scanned in the Normal zone by the kswapd background reclaimer (/proc/vmstat pgscan_kswapd_normal). Older per-zone kernel name; newer kernels renamed or removed it, and then the value is recorded as not present rather than 0. Counter: delta / elapsed s.

Pages scanned in the Normal zone by direct (synchronous, allocation-stalling) reclaim (/proc/vmstat pgscan_direct_normal). Older per-zone kernel name; newer kernels renamed or removed it, and then the value is recorded as not present rather than 0. Counter: delta / elapsed s.
Pages reclaimed by freeing inodes during direct reclaim (/proc/vmstat pginodesteal). Counter: take the difference between samples and divide by elapsed seconds for a rate.
Slab cache objects scanned by the shrinkers during reclaim (/proc/vmstat slabs_scanned). Counter: take the difference between samples and divide by elapsed seconds for a rate.
Pages reclaimed by kswapd (/proc/vmstat kswapd_steal). Old kernel name, removed in later kernels, where it is recorded as not present. Counter: delta / elapsed s.
Pages reclaimed by kswapd by freeing inodes (/proc/vmstat kswapd_inodesteal). Counter: take the difference between samples and divide by elapsed seconds for a rate.
Number of kswapd reclaim passes (/proc/vmstat pageoutrun). Counter: take the difference between samples and divide by elapsed seconds for a rate.

Times an allocation stalled to do direct reclaim (/proc/vmstat allocstall). Newer kernels split it per zone (allocstall_normal etc.) and then this key is recorded as not present. Counter: delta / elapsed s.
Pages rotated to the tail of the inactive list after writeback (/proc/vmstat pgrotated). Counter: take the difference between samples and divide by elapsed seconds for a rate.
Transparent huge pages successfully allocated at page-fault time (/proc/vmstat thp_fault_alloc). Counter: take the difference between samples and divide by elapsed seconds for a rate.

Page faults that wanted a transparent huge page but fell back to small pages (/proc/vmstat thp_fault_fallback); high rates mean fragmented memory. Counter: take the difference between samples and divide by elapsed seconds for a rate.
Huge pages allocated by khugepaged to collapse small pages into a THP (/proc/vmstat thp_collapse_alloc). Counter: take the difference between samples and divide by elapsed seconds for a rate.
khugepaged huge page allocations that failed (/proc/vmstat thp_collapse_alloc_failed). Counter: take the difference between samples and divide by elapsed seconds for a rate.
Transparent huge pages split into small pages (/proc/vmstat thp_split). Newer kernels renamed it (thp_split_page), and then it is recorded as not present. Counter: delta / elapsed s.

Intel Data Center GPU Max (Ponte Vecchio) metrics from Intel XPU Manager (build flag --enable-intel-gpu). Default backend runs xpumcli discovery + dump (1 s sample) each collect; opt-in libxpum (dlopen) via intel_gpu_backend=libxpum or HPCPERFSTATS_INTEL_GPU_BACKEND. Backend failures keep rows with BACKEND_ERROR/BACKOFF sentinels.
XPUM device id as a decimal string, e.g. 0 (Stampede3 PVC nodes: 0..3). If discovery never succeeded, rows are 0..N-1 where N is the Data Center GPU Max PCI functions found in sysfs.
GPU utilization in %, rounded. xpumcli dump column GPU Utilization, or libxpum XPUM_STATS_GPU_UTILIZATION (0). Gauge for the XPUM sample (about 1 s on xpumcli).
Memory capacity utilization in %: (physical - free) / physical per XPUM, not bandwidth. xpumcli column GPU Memory Utilization or XPUM_STATS_MEMORY_UTILIZATION (9). Instantaneous gauge.

Total GPU memory in MiB (labelled MB). libxpum: device property MEMORY_PHYSICAL_SIZE_BYTE. xpumcli: DERIVED as used / (gpu_mem_util / 100), so approximate and 0 when utilization is 0 or missing. Gauge.
Used GPU memory in MiB (labelled MB). xpumcli column GPU Memory Used (already MiB), or libxpum XPUM_STATS_MEMORY_USED (8, bytes / 1048576). Instantaneous gauge.
GPU package power in W, rounded. xpumcli column GPU Power; libxpum XPUM_STATS_POWER (4), taking the larger of the device value and the sum over tiles (never one tile). Gauge over the XPUM sample.

GPU core temperature in C. xpumcli column GPU Core Temperature or XPUM_STATS_GPU_CORE_TEMPERATURE (7); falls back to GPU memory temperature (XPUM_STATS_MEMORY_TEMPERATURE, 30) when core is missing. Instantaneous gauge.
Actual GPU frequency in MHz (named for schema kinship with nvidia_gpu). xpumcli column GPU Frequency or XPUM_STATS_GPU_FREQUENCY (6). Gauge over the XPUM sample.

EU (execution unit) array active %, the Intel analog of NVIDIA sm_active. xpumcli column EU Array Active or XPUM_STATS_EU_ACTIVE (1). Gauge. NOT_PRESENT when XPUM prints N/A (e.g. GFX firmware below XPUM minimum).
Memory bandwidth utilization in % of peak. xpumcli column Memory Bandwidth or XPUM_STATS_MEMORY_BANDWIDTH (10). Gauge over the XPUM sample.

PCIe read bytes from libxpum XPUM_STATS_PCIE_READ (34, unit B), published as XPUM returns it (treated as monotonic counter, E). libxpum backend only: always NOT_BUILT on the default xpumcli backend, which has only throughput.

PCIe write bytes from libxpum XPUM_STATS_PCIE_WRITE (35, unit B), published as XPUM returns it (treated as monotonic counter, E). libxpum backend only: always NOT_BUILT on the default xpumcli backend.

Xe Link (GPU-to-GPU fabric) received bytes: sum over links of accumulated RECEIVED_COUNTER from xpumGetFabricThroughputStats. Cumulative counter (E). libxpum backend only: NOT_BUILT on the default xpumcli backend.

Xe Link (GPU-to-GPU fabric) transmitted bytes: sum over links of accumulated TRANSMITTED_COUNTER from xpumGetFabricThroughputStats. Cumulative counter (E). libxpum backend only: NOT_BUILT on the default xpumcli backend.

Throttle indicator. xpumcli: 0/1 flag, 1 when the dump Throttle column is not Not Throttled. libxpum: raw XPUM_STATS_FREQUENCY_THROTTLE_REASON_GPU (38, zes throttle-reason bitmask) or else FREQUENCY_THROTTLE (31, % time); neither is in the collector's XPUM_METRICS list, so often NOT_PRESENT.
Number of XPUM-discovered Intel GPUs on the node; same value on every device row. Gauge. Slow key: only in @full rows.

Compute engine group utilization in %, max over tiles (a 2-tile Max 1550 reports the busier tile). xpumcli column Compute engine group utilization or XPUM_STATS_ENGINE_GROUP_COMPUTE_ALL_UTILIZATION (15). Gauge.

Per-socket RAPL energy on Intel SKX/CLX/ICX/SPR/EMR/GNR/SRF (and client Skylake), x86 builds only. Each domain reads the perf power PMU event (energy-pkg/-cores/-gpu/-ram, scaled) on one CPU of the socket, else the powercap energy_uj zone; no MSR access. Values are running totals in mJ since daemon start, modulo 2^32.
CPU package (socket) id from topology/physical_package_id, e.g. 0. One row per socket.

Energy of the whole processor package (cores, caches, uncore; perf energy-pkg, else powercap package zone), mJ running total modulo 2^32. delta mJ / (1000 x elapsed s) = watts. Sum rows for all sockets.

Energy of the cores power plane PP0 (perf energy-cores, else powercap core zone), mJ modulo 2^32. delta mJ / (1000 x elapsed s) = watts. Many server CPUs do not expose this domain and emit -2 NOT_PRESENT.

Energy of power plane PP1, normally a client integrated GPU (perf energy-gpu, else powercap uncore zone), mJ modulo 2^32. delta mJ / (1000 x elapsed s) = watts. Server CPUs usually lack it and emit -2 NOT_PRESENT.
Energy of the socket's attached DRAM (perf energy-ram, else powercap dram zone), mJ modulo 2^32. delta mJ / (1000 x elapsed s) = watts. -2 NOT_PRESENT when the domain is not exposed.

Intel Emerald Rapids memory-controller CAS counts via direct perf on every uncore_imc_<N> PMU (plus uncore_hbm_<N> on HBM parts such as SPR Max); x86 builds, enabled only when the runtime CPU is EMR. Each row sums its PMU cpumask CPUs (one per socket), so it covers all sockets (about 2x pre-3.1 values on 2-socket nodes).
mbox<N> for DDR PMU uncore_imc_<N> (e.g. mbox0), and hbm<N> for HBM PMU uncore_hbm_<N> (e.g. hbm0, up to 32) on HBM parts. Rows cover all sockets.

DRAM read CAS commands on this IMC channel (sysfs cas_count_read, else raw 0x05/0xcf), 64 bytes each, modulo 2^48. Sum delta over rows x 64 / elapsed s = DRAM read bytes/s. -2 NOT_PRESENT on hbm<N> rows.

DRAM write CAS commands on this IMC channel (sysfs cas_count_write, else raw 0x05/0xf0), 64 bytes each, modulo 2^48. Sum delta over rows x 64 / elapsed s = DRAM write bytes/s. -2 NOT_PRESENT on hbm<N> rows.

HBM read CAS commands on uncore_hbm_<N> (raw 0x05/0xcf), 32 bytes each, modulo 2^48. Filled only on hbm<N> rows (mbox rows -2 NOT_PRESENT); no hbm rows without HBM. Sum delta x 32 / elapsed s = HBM read bytes/s.

HBM write CAS commands on uncore_hbm_<N> (raw 0x05/0xf0), 32 bytes each, modulo 2^48. Filled only on hbm<N> rows (mbox rows -2 NOT_PRESENT); no hbm rows without HBM. Sum delta x 32 / elapsed s = HBM write bytes/s.

Nanoseconds this row's CAS events were enabled, summed over its events and cpumask CPUs, 64-bit. delta running / delta enabled = share of time the counters ran; below 1 the CAS counts are scaled estimates. No solo key for uncore.

Nanoseconds this row's CAS events actually ran on a counter, summed over its events and cpumask CPUs, 64-bit. delta running / delta enabled = share of time the counters ran; below 1 the CAS counts are scaled estimates. No solo key for uncore.

Intel Granite Rapids memory-controller CAS counts via direct perf on every uncore_imc_<N> PMU; x86 builds, enabled only when the runtime CPU is GNR. Each row sums its PMU cpumask CPUs (one per socket), so it covers all sockets (about 2x pre-3.1 values on 2-socket nodes).
mbox<N> for PMU uncore_imc_<N>, e.g. mbox0. Rows cover all sockets.

DRAM read CAS commands on this IMC channel (sysfs cas_count_read, else raw 0x05/0xcf, scheduler 0 only (CAS_COUNT_SCH0; scheduler 1 is not counted)), 64 bytes each, modulo 2^48. Sum delta over rows x 64 / elapsed s = DRAM read bytes/s.

DRAM write CAS commands on this IMC channel (sysfs cas_count_write, else raw 0x05/0xf0, scheduler 0 only (CAS_COUNT_SCH0; scheduler 1 is not counted)), 64 bytes each, modulo 2^48. Sum delta over rows x 64 / elapsed s = DRAM write bytes/s.

Nanoseconds this row's CAS events were enabled, summed over its events and cpumask CPUs, 64-bit. delta running / delta enabled = share of time the counters ran; below 1 the CAS counts are scaled estimates. No solo key for uncore.

Nanoseconds this row's CAS events actually ran on a counter, summed over its events and cpumask CPUs, 64-bit. delta running / delta enabled = share of time the counters ran; below 1 the CAS counts are scaled estimates. No solo key for uncore.

Intel Ice Lake server memory-controller CAS counts via direct perf on every uncore_imc_<N> PMU; x86 builds, enabled only when the runtime CPU is ICX. Each row sums its PMU cpumask CPUs (one per socket), so it covers all sockets (about 2x pre-3.1 values on 2-socket nodes).
mdev<N> for PMU uncore_imc_<N>, e.g. mdev0. Rows cover all sockets.
DRAM read CAS commands on this IMC channel (sysfs cas_count_read, else raw 0x04/0x0f), 64 bytes each, modulo 2^48. Sum delta over rows x 64 / elapsed s = DRAM read bytes/s.
DRAM write CAS commands on this IMC channel (sysfs cas_count_write, else raw 0x04/0x30), 64 bytes each, modulo 2^48. Sum delta over rows x 64 / elapsed s = DRAM write bytes/s.

Nanoseconds this row's CAS events were enabled, summed over its events and cpumask CPUs, 64-bit. delta running / delta enabled = share of time the counters ran; below 1 the CAS counts are scaled estimates. No solo key for uncore.

Nanoseconds this row's CAS events actually ran on a counter, summed over its events and cpumask CPUs, 64-bit. delta running / delta enabled = share of time the counters ran; below 1 the CAS counts are scaled estimates. No solo key for uncore.

Intel Skylake-SP and Cascade Lake memory-controller CAS counts via direct perf on every uncore_imc_<N> PMU; x86 builds, enabled only when the runtime CPU is SKX/CLX. Each row sums its PMU cpumask CPUs (one per socket), so it covers all sockets (about 2x pre-3.1 values on 2-socket nodes).
mbox<N> for PMU uncore_imc_<N>, e.g. mbox0. Rows cover all sockets.
DRAM read CAS commands on this IMC channel (sysfs cas_count_read, else raw 0x04/0x03), 64 bytes each, modulo 2^48. Sum delta over rows x 64 / elapsed s = DRAM read bytes/s.
DRAM write CAS commands on this IMC channel (sysfs cas_count_write, else raw 0x04/0x0c), 64 bytes each, modulo 2^48. Sum delta over rows x 64 / elapsed s = DRAM write bytes/s.
DRAM row activate count placeholder: no hardware-verified event encoding, so this key always emits -10 NOT_BUILT. Do not use.
DRAM precharge-on-page-miss count placeholder: no hardware-verified event encoding, so this key always emits -10 NOT_BUILT. Do not use.

Nanoseconds this row's CAS events were enabled, summed over its events and cpumask CPUs, 64-bit. delta running / delta enabled = share of time the counters ran; below 1 the CAS counts are scaled estimates. No solo key for uncore.

Nanoseconds this row's CAS events actually ran on a counter, summed over its events and cpumask CPUs, 64-bit. delta running / delta enabled = share of time the counters ran; below 1 the CAS counts are scaled estimates. No solo key for uncore.

Intel Sapphire Rapids memory-controller CAS counts via direct perf on every uncore_imc_<N> PMU (plus uncore_hbm_<N> on HBM parts such as SPR Max); x86 builds, enabled only when the runtime CPU is SPR. Each row sums its PMU cpumask CPUs (one per socket), so it covers all sockets (about 2x pre-3.1 values on 2-socket nodes).
mbox<N> for DDR PMU uncore_imc_<N> (e.g. mbox0), and hbm<N> for HBM PMU uncore_hbm_<N> (e.g. hbm0, up to 32) on HBM parts. Rows cover all sockets.

DRAM read CAS commands on this IMC channel (sysfs cas_count_read, else raw 0x05/0xcf), 64 bytes each, modulo 2^48. Sum delta over rows x 64 / elapsed s = DRAM read bytes/s. -2 NOT_PRESENT on hbm<N> rows.

DRAM write CAS commands on this IMC channel (sysfs cas_count_write, else raw 0x05/0xf0), 64 bytes each, modulo 2^48. Sum delta over rows x 64 / elapsed s = DRAM write bytes/s. -2 NOT_PRESENT on hbm<N> rows.

HBM read CAS commands on uncore_hbm_<N> (raw 0x05/0xcf), 32 bytes each, modulo 2^48. Filled only on hbm<N> rows (mbox rows -2 NOT_PRESENT); no hbm rows without HBM. Sum delta x 32 / elapsed s = HBM read bytes/s.

HBM write CAS commands on uncore_hbm_<N> (raw 0x05/0xf0), 32 bytes each, modulo 2^48. Filled only on hbm<N> rows (mbox rows -2 NOT_PRESENT); no hbm rows without HBM. Sum delta x 32 / elapsed s = HBM write bytes/s.

Nanoseconds this row's CAS events were enabled, summed over its events and cpumask CPUs, 64-bit. delta running / delta enabled = share of time the counters ran; below 1 the CAS counts are scaled estimates. No solo key for uncore.

Nanoseconds this row's CAS events actually ran on a counter, summed over its events and cpumask CPUs, 64-bit. delta running / delta enabled = share of time the counters ran; below 1 the CAS counts are scaled estimates. No solo key for uncore.

Intel Sierra Forest memory-controller CAS counts via direct perf on every uncore_imc_<N> PMU; x86 builds, enabled only when the runtime CPU is SRF. Each row sums its PMU cpumask CPUs (one per socket), so it covers all sockets (about 2x pre-3.1 values on 2-socket nodes).
mbox<N> for PMU uncore_imc_<N>, e.g. mbox0. Rows cover all sockets.

DRAM read CAS commands on this IMC channel (sysfs cas_count_read, else raw 0x05/0xcf, scheduler 0 only (CAS_COUNT_SCH0; scheduler 1 is not counted)), 64 bytes each, modulo 2^48. Sum delta over rows x 64 / elapsed s = DRAM read bytes/s.

DRAM write CAS commands on this IMC channel (sysfs cas_count_write, else raw 0x05/0xf0, scheduler 0 only (CAS_COUNT_SCH0; scheduler 1 is not counted)), 64 bytes each, modulo 2^48. Sum delta over rows x 64 / elapsed s = DRAM write bytes/s.

Nanoseconds this row's CAS events were enabled, summed over its events and cpumask CPUs, 64-bit. delta running / delta enabled = share of time the counters ran; below 1 the CAS counts are scaled estimates. No solo key for uncore.

Nanoseconds this row's CAS events actually ran on a counter, summed over its events and cpumask CPUs, 64-bit. delta running / delta enabled = share of time the counters ran; below 1 the CAS counts are scaled estimates. No solo key for uncore.

Lustre client VFS activity and capacity per mounted filesystem. Op and byte counters come from the llite instance stats file (/proc/fs/lustre/llite/<inst>/stats; debugfs /sys/kernel/debug/lustre/llite on 2.15+); capacity from /sys/fs/lustre/llite/<inst>/kbytes*, files*. One row per filesystem in every sample; built with --enable-lustre (default on).

Filesystem client LOV name: the /proc/fs/lustre/lov entry with its trailing -<16 hex superblock> suffix removed, e.g. scratch-clilov (from scratch-clilov-ffff8881a2b3c400). The llite instance is matched to it by that superblock suffix. Not a mount path.

Count of read() calls handled by the Lustre client on this Lustre mount, from llite stats line read sample count. Counter: difference between samples / elapsed seconds = ops/s. Lustre omits zero lines, so an absent line is recorded as 0.

Count of write() calls handled by the Lustre client on this Lustre mount, from llite stats line write sample count. Counter: difference between samples / elapsed seconds = ops/s. Lustre omits zero lines, so an absent line is recorded as 0.

Bytes read by applications through this Lustre mount, from llite stats line read_bytes sum field (bytes). Counter: difference between samples / elapsed seconds = bytes/s. Lustre omits zero lines, so an absent line is recorded as 0.

Bytes written by applications through this Lustre mount, from llite stats line write_bytes sum field (bytes). Counter: difference between samples / elapsed seconds = bytes/s. Lustre omits zero lines, so an absent line is recorded as 0.

Bytes moved by O_DIRECT reads on this Lustre mount, from llite stats line direct_read sum field (count if the line has no sum). Counter: difference between samples / elapsed seconds = bytes/s. Lustre omits zero lines, so an absent line is recorded as 0.

Bytes moved by O_DIRECT writes on this Lustre mount, from llite stats line direct_write sum field (count if the line has no sum). Counter: difference between samples / elapsed seconds = bytes/s. Lustre omits zero lines, so an absent line is recorded as 0.

Value of llite stats line osc_read sum field (bytes; count if no sum), the Lustre module's count of read bytes passed to the OSC layer; exact semantics are Lustre's. Counter: difference between samples / elapsed seconds = bytes/s. Lustre omits zero lines, so an absent line is recorded as 0.

Value of llite stats line osc_write sum field (bytes; count if no sum), the Lustre module's count of write bytes passed to the OSC layer; exact semantics are Lustre's. Counter: difference between samples / elapsed seconds = bytes/s. Lustre omits zero lines, so an absent line is recorded as 0.

Writes that hit a page already dirty in the client cache, from llite stats line dirty_pages_hits sample count (as defined by the Lustre module). Counter: difference between samples / elapsed seconds. Lustre omits zero lines, so an absent line is recorded as 0.

Writes to a page not already dirty in the client cache, from llite stats line dirty_pages_misses sample count (as defined by the Lustre module). Counter: difference between samples / elapsed seconds. Lustre omits zero lines, so an absent line is recorded as 0.

Total filesystem capacity of the Lustre filesystem as the client sees it, from /sys/fs/lustre/llite/<inst>/kbytestotal (KiB x 1024 = bytes). Gauge: read as is.
Free space (including root-reserved) of the Lustre filesystem as the client sees it, from /sys/fs/lustre/llite/<inst>/kbytesfree (KiB x 1024 = bytes). Gauge: read as is.
